source_name: Finančná správa SR — Portál FS, sekcia eKasa / pokladnice ERP
why_relevant: Official operational and regulatory pages for the eKasa scheme: certified cash-register/ORP-VRP requirements, technical specifications for cash-register vendors, obligations of merchants. Directly relevant to the SK POS/terminal ecosystem (who may supply certified devices, what data flows to the state) and to any change in acceptance of cashless payments at the till.

source_name: Portál FS — podpora.financnasprava.sk (knowledge base / FAQ on cash registers)
why_relevant: Authoritative FAQ layer explaining exemptions from eKasa obligation, deposit/withdrawal registration of cash, and practical scope of the scheme. Useful for correctly interpreting the coverage and gaps of eKasa aggregates (i.e. what share of cash trade is NOT captured).

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — DATAcube. public statistical database
why_relevant: Core national statistical database: retail turnover (tržby vo vnútornom obchode) monthly indices and quarterly absolute values, wholesale, accommodation and food services, household income/expenditure, ICT use. Provides the macro denominators for payment-market sizing that NBS does not publish (turnover by NACE, by region, time series).

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — STATdata (successor public database to DATAcube)
why_relevant: ŠÚ SR created STATdata in 2024 as the modern replacement for DATAcube; new cubes are being created only in STATdata while migration proceeds, so any long-term collection pipeline must track this migration or it will silently stop receiving new tables.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — Informatívne správy: Tržby vo vnútornom obchode (monthly/quarterly releases)
why_relevant: The recurring monthly commentary releases on internal-trade turnover (retail excl. motor vehicles, wholesale, accommodation, gastro) — narrative plus headline figures ahead of the full cube. High-frequency signal on the transaction base that card and cash payments ride on.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — Zisťovanie o využívaní IKT v domácnostiach a jednotlivcami (ICT household survey)
why_relevant: Annual EU-harmonised household survey (~5,200 households) covering online shopping, e-government interaction, digital skills, electronic ID use. It is the public evidence base for e-commerce penetration and online payment behaviour in SK at population level — a demand-side complement to eKasa's supply-side data.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — Elektronický zber údajov (zber.statistics.sk) survey catalogue
why_relevant: Catalogue of every statistical survey ŠÚ SR runs, with questionnaires and legal basis. Reading the questionnaires reveals which payment/cash variables are actually collected (and therefore what could be requested or published later) — a pointer that expands the actor and variable map well beyond what is published as headline tables.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — Open data section (portal hub)
why_relevant: Entry point describing ŠÚ SR's open-data offering and linking to the API help; the reliable route to discover new machine-readable products and format changes.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR — Obmedzenie platieb v hotovosti (cash payment limit)
why_relevant: The ministry's dedicated page on the statutory cash-payment ceiling (zákon o obmedzení platieb v hotovosti) — the single most direct policy lever pushing SK transactions from cash to cards/transfers. Tracks thresholds, exemptions, guidance and any amendment, including alignment with the EU AML cash-limit regime.

source_name: Inštitút finančnej politiky (IFP), MF SR — Publikácie / Ekonomické analýzy
why_relevant: MF SR's in-house analytical unit publishes commentaries and analyses on the VAT gap, tax collection efficiency and the effects of measures such as eKasa — the closest thing to a quantified public estimate of undeclared cash trade in Slovakia, produced by an actor with administrative microdata access.

source_name: IFP — Manuál: Daňová medzera na DPH (VAT gap methodology)
why_relevant: Methodological manual for how Slovakia estimates the VAT gap; the manual and its updates are the reference for interpreting claims that eKasa or cashless-payment obligations reduced the shadow cash economy. Directly supports cash-usage analysis with an auditable method.

source_name: Útvar hodnoty za peniaze (ÚHP), MF SR — Analýzy
why_relevant: The Value-for-Money unit reviews public spending and IT/administrative projects; revenue-administration and digitalisation reviews (of which eKasa-type systems are typical subjects) surface cost, coverage and effectiveness figures unavailable elsewhere. Second analytical actor inside MF SR alongside IFP.

source_name: Open Data MF SR (opendata.mfsr.sk)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance open-data platform publishing datasets of MF SR and its subordinate budget organisations under an open licence in machine-readable form, with an OData access layer. Useful for fiscal aggregates and for tracing state spending on payment/IT infrastructure.

source_name: Ministerstvo investícií, regionálneho rozvoja a informatizácie SR (MIRRI) — Otvorené údaje / Centrálna dátová kancelária
why_relevant: Governance owner of the SK open-data regime; publishes the rules, quality standards and roadmap that determine what fiscal and statistical bodies must publish. Useful for anticipating future data availability (and for arguing for access when a dataset is missing).

source_name: Najvyšší kontrolný úrad SR (NKÚ) — Zoznam aktuálnych kontrol (ongoing audits register)
why_relevant: NKÚ publishes the list of audits currently under way together with interim results. This is an early-warning pointer: an audit opened on Finančná správa, eKasa or tax collection signals that a detailed public report with hard numbers on cash-register coverage and enforcement will follow.

source_name: NKÚ SR — Stanoviská k návrhu štátneho rozpočtu (opinions on the draft state budget)
why_relevant: NKÚ's annual opinion on the draft state budget routinely scrutinises tax-revenue assumptions, including the assumed yield from anti-evasion measures such as eKasa and cashless-payment obligations — an independent public critique of the fiscal authorities' own claims about cash-vs-card at the till.

source_name: Národná rada SR — parliamentary document repository (dôvodové správy, Parlamentný inštitút)
why_relevant: Explanatory memoranda (dôvodové správy) and Parliamentary Institute analyses attached to bills such as zákon č. 384/2025 Z. z. o evidencii tržieb (eKasa successor, effective 1.1.2026) and the cash-payment-limit law contain impact estimates, merchant counts and cash-share assumptions that are not published anywhere else. Legislative pipeline = forward view of SK acceptance rules.

source_name: Finančná správa SR — press releases / tlačové správy on eKasa enforcement and cashless-payment compliance
why_relevant: The tax authority periodically discloses operational numbers not in the open-data files — e.g. total cash registers in eKasa versus the estimated population of registers, daily receipt volumes, and targeted enforcement campaigns on sectors with a high cash share (gastro, accommodation, personal care, construction, private clinics) and on compliance with new cashless-acceptance rules. These are the qualitative markers of where cash is concentrated in SK.

source_name: Štatistický úrad SR — susr.sk PDF export service (ExportPdf2)
why_relevant: A stable, document-GUID-addressable PDF rendering of ŠÚ SR portal pages and releases. Because the main portal's WebSphere URLs are volatile and hostile to crawlers, this export endpoint is a practical collection workaround for archiving releases such as the retail-turnover commentaries and the Databázy status page.

source_name: SBA — Členovia / Members list
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of ~24 members (full members = banks/branches; associate members = infrastructure firms). Reveals every deposit-taker worth monitoring plus infrastructure actors such as Regional Card Processing Centre, Nexi Group, Centrálny depozitár cenných papierov SR, Eximbanka — a snowball seed for the whole SK entity map.

source_name: SBA — Novinky / press releases
why_relevant: Association press stream carrying market-wide aggregates that individual banks do not publish (instant-payment adoption, digital payment share of in-store purchases, terminal counts, cash usage commentary) plus sector positions on levies/transaction tax.

source_name: Národný plán zavedenia okamžitých platieb v SR (NBS + SBA + MF SR + Štátna pokladnica)
why_relevant: The national instant-payment scheme plan jointly produced by the banking association and the central bank; names participating PSPs, milestones and adoption thresholds. Core artefact for the national IPS scheme body dimension of this cell.

source_name: NBS — Platobné systémy (payment systems: TARGET2-SK / TIPS, SIPS operator pages)
why_relevant: NBS is the operator/host of the Slovak clearing infrastructure (historically SIPS retail clearing, now TARGET services incl. TIPS for instant payments). Operator pages carry participant lists and throughput/turnover reporting as a by-product of running the rails.

source_name: NBS — TARGET2-SK a SIPS (historical clearing operator page)
why_relevant: Documents the structural transition of SK interbank clearing (SIPS retail vs TARGET2 large-value after euro adoption 2009) and participant counts. Needed to interpret long time series of transaction volumes.

source_name: Slovak Banking Credit Bureau, s.r.o. (SBCB) — operator of Spoločný register bankových informácií (SRBI)
why_relevant: Shared bank-owned credit infrastructure (founded by Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB and Tatra banka with CRIF). Participant/member list identifies all lending banks; any published register statistics are market-wide credit aggregates unavailable per bank.

source_name: Non Banking Credit Bureau (NBCB) / NRKI — Nebankový register klientskych informácií
why_relevant: Sister shared-infrastructure body for the non-bank lending side (~32 members, leasing/instalment/consumer finance), exchanging data with SRBI since 2015. Its member list is the pointer surface for non-bank credit providers — relevant because run sector=both.

source_name: CRIF – Slovak Credit Bureau, s.r.o.
why_relevant: Technical operator behind both SK credit registers and a commercial data vendor; publishes credit-market commentary and aggregate indicators derived from register coverage of >99% of the SK credit market.

source_name: Regional Card Processing Centre, s.r.o. (RPC) — SBA associate member
why_relevant: Shared card-processing infrastructure headquartered in Bratislava (Raiffeisen group), processing roughly 8 million debit/credit cards across ~9 CEE banks incl. Tatra banka, and connecting terminals and wallet schemes. Rare visibility into SK card issuing/acquiring processing capacity and estate.

source_name: Centrálny depozitár cenných papierov SR (CDCP) — SBA associate member, market infrastructure
why_relevant: National CSD and an SBA associate member; publishes settlement/participant information. Secondary for card/ATM topics but part of the shared market-infrastructure map and a participant-list pointer to SK banks.
